title: The West Virginia madam who wanted a record the band had forgotten
summary: A woman who brought her girls to hear them demanded a tune on her jukebox; the band found the record, relearned it from playback and played it for her.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yes, yes. You had to. I'll tell you why, because I remember, we were in West Virginia one night, and we were playing, and some woman had a -- she had a house. She closed her girls up and brought them all with her and --

to hear us play, and she was a fine looking woman, and had some fine looking gals, and she had plenty of money, and she walked in there and sat down, and she asked for a certain tune. So I said, 'I'm very sorry.' "What do you mean you're sorry?" I don't have that. She said, "well, you recorded it." You say well no, I don't think so. You've got me" -- she said don't tell me. I have it in my joint on the jukebox. Oh God!

Fats say, you do? (Laughs.) Fats starts thinking. She say I have my own business back in such and such a town. I closed up tonight and brought my girls with me because I wanted to hear you play. He says, what's the name of the song? La, nm, nm, nm, nm, and so he -- so he called us out. He say hey fellows, did we record the splk-ll-blkk? The guys say I think. We don't remember. She said don't tell me! I have it on my jukebox. So he sent his valet out. He says go out and look for this. He wrote it on paper, on a piece, and the guy came back with the record.

Fats took it, we had -- took it in the back room, in the dressing room, and put it on his machine, played it. We started listening. (Laughs.) He says well I'll be damned! I think that sounds like me. And that sounds like
me. And that sounds like me. He said well we did make it, didn't we? You know. (Laughs.) Find out it was a record.

Now, we had to stay back there and learn it all over again and go out and play it for this woman. This woman come all these miles to hear the -- you know, she didn't want no stuff. You know, we had to play the damn --
Yeah. And so Fats apologized. We came out and played it for her. That's it! That's what I want! Don't tell me.
